description: The chart illustrates how average model attention is proportionally distributed across three input segments (Context, Generated Response, and Other) for two experimental conditions, shown as horizontal stacked bars. The category axis is the vertical axis with two labeled conditions, “Ours” on top and “Standard” below, and the value axis is the horizontal axis representing percentage share (a linear percent scale), with each stacked bar spanning the full 100% width and segment values printed inside the bars. For “Ours,” the stacked bar contains a blue Context segment labeled 60.6%, followed by an orange Generated Response segment labeled 31.7%, and a green Other segment labeled 7.7%. For “Standard,” the stacked bar contains a blue Context segment labeled 23.6%, followed by an orange Generated Response segment labeled 51.1%, and a green Other segment labeled 25.3%. The stacking order is consistent (Context then Generated Response then Other from left to right), the bars are not shown as sorted beyond the displayed top-to-bottom condition order, and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the internal percentage annotations and the legend mapping blue/orange/green to the three segments.
caption_used: The bar chart presents the average proportional attention the model allocates to three input segments—Context, Generated Response, and Other (e.g., system prompts)—across two experimental conditions: 'Ours' and 'Standard.' The vertical axis denotes the experimental conditions, while the horizontal axis represents the percentage distribution. In the 'Ours' condition, the model predominantly attends to Context (approximately 60.6%), with Generated Response comprising roughly 31.7% and Other stabilizing at 15.2%. Conversely, the 'Standard' condition reveals a markedly reduced focus on Context (23.6%), while Generated Response consistently surpasses other segments at 51.1%, and Other accounts for 25.3%. Notably, the 'Ours' approach demonstrates a substantially diminished reliance on system prompts and ancillary inputs compared to the 'Standard' method, suggesting enhanced contextual integration during generation.
